Hi Mark,

That `newformatLong` function was a custom function that's not included in the example and likely doesn't work any more even if you had it. The current `formatLong` function is to be preferred, and I don't suspect `visit` is a yearlySiteCov.

You'll need to modify your `visit` variable to reflect your primary/secondary sampling scheme. You have 10 possible visits to a site (5 primary periods, each with 2 secondary samples), so `visit` would need to take values in 1:10 across all sites. That is, primary period 1 (2014) with be associated with visits 1 & 2, primary period 2 (2015) will be associated with visits 3 & 4, and so on.

I've not intensively checked this, but the following should set up your data to be ready for `formatLong`:

library(unmarked)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

FWCPdata <- read.csv("~/FWS_Projects/sandbox/Data/FWCPDataLongTsp.csv", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  # Drop records with no response; we'll complete data set below
  filter(!is.na(y))

# Explicitly define the sampling scheme so we can complete the data set with missing values later
sampling_scheme <- expand.grid(spp.6 = unique(FWCPdata$spp.6),
                               visit = 1:10,
                               site = unique(FWCPdata$site),
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

FWCPdata <- FWCPdata %>%
  arrange(spp.6, site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = dmy(date), # Convert string to date
         doy = yday(date), # Day of year variable; I think this is what you want instead of the 'Julian' function
         year = lubridate::year(date),
         visit = visit + ((year - min(year)) * 2 )) %>% # Number visits assuming 5 primary (yearly), 2 secondary periods
  # Use sampling scheme to fill the data set with NAs, keeping the visit sequence correct
  left_join(sampling_scheme, .) %>%
  # Rearrange columns for unmarked
  select(site, visit, y, spp.6, place.1:doy) %>%
  # Rearrange rows for human eyes
  arrange(spp.6, site, visit)

Hi Mark,

That `newformatLong` function was a custom function that's not included in the example and likely doesn't work any more even if you had it. The current `formatLong` function is to be preferred, and I don't suspect `visit` is a yearlySiteCov.

You'll need to modify your `visit` variable to reflect your primary/secondary sampling scheme. You have 10 possible visits to a site (5 primary periods, each with 2 secondary samples), so `visit` would need to take values in 1:10 across all sites. That is, primary period 1 (2014) with be associated with visits 1 & 2, primary period 2 (2015) will be associated with visits 3 & 4, and so on.

I've not intensively checked this, but the following should set up your data to be ready for `formatLong`:

library(unmarked)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

FWCPdata <- read.csv("~/FWS_Projects/sandbox/Data/FWCPDataLongTsp.csv", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  # Drop records with no response; we'll complete data set below
  filter(!is.na(y))

# Explicitly define the sampling scheme so we can complete the data set with missing values later
sampling_scheme <- expand.grid(spp.6 = unique(FWCPdata$spp.6),
                               visit = 1:10,
                               site = unique(FWCPdata$site),
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

FWCPdata <- FWCPdata %>%
  arrange(spp.6, site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = dmy(date), # Convert string to date
         doy = yday(date), # Day of year variable; I think this is what you want instead of the 'Julian' function
         year = lubridate::year(date),
         visit = visit + ((year - min(year)) * 2 )) %>% # Number visits assuming 5 primary (yearly), 2 secondary periods
  # Use sampling scheme to fill the data set with NAs, keeping the visit sequence correct
  left_join(sampling_scheme, .) %>%
  # Rearrange columns for unmarked
  select(site, visit, y, spp.6, place.1:doy) %>%
  # Rearrange rows for human eyes
  arrange(spp.6, site, visit)

That `newformatLong` function was a custom function that's not included in the example and likely doesn't work any more even if you had it. The current `formatLong` function is to be preferred, and I don't suspect `visit` is a yearlySiteCov.

You'll need to modify your `visit` variable to reflect your primary/secondary sampling scheme. You have 10 possible visits to a site (5 primary periods, each with 2 secondary samples), so `visit` would need to take values in 1:10 across all sites. That is, primary period 1 (2014) with be associated with visits 1 & 2, primary period 2 (2015) will be associated with visits 3 & 4, and so on.

I've not intensively checked this, but the following should set up your data to be ready for `formatLong`:

library(unmarked)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

FWCPdata <- read.csv("~/FWS_Projects/sandbox/Data/FWCPDataLongTsp.csv", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  # Drop records with no response; we'll complete data set below
  filter(!is.na(y))

# Explicitly define the sampling scheme so we can complete the data set with missing values later
sampling_scheme <- expand.grid(spp.6 = unique(FWCPdata$spp.6),
                               visit = 1:10,
                               site = unique(FWCPdata$site),
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

FWCPdata <- FWCPdata %>%
  arrange(spp.6, site, date) %>%
  mutate(date = dmy(date), # Convert string to date
         doy = yday(date), # Day of year variable; I think this is what you want instead of the 'Julian' function
         year = lubridate::year(date),
         visit = visit + ((year - min(year)) * 2 )) %>% # Number visits assuming 5 primary (yearly), 2 secondary periods
  # Use sampling scheme to fill the data set with NAs, keeping the visit sequence correct
  left_join(sampling_scheme, .) %>%
  # Rearrange columns for unmarked
  select(site, visit, y, spp.6, place.1:doy) %>%
  # Rearrange rows for human eyes
